questions.question: How was the structure of the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rectangle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro is one of the most famous structures found at the site of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• It is a large, rectangular tank located in the citadel area, which suggests its importance for ritualistic or ceremonial purposes.
 
• The tank measures approximately 12 meters long, 7 meters wide, and 2.4 meters deep.
 
• The structure is made of finely fitted bricks and features a series of steps leading down to the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjo-daro**

 
 
• Mohenjo-daro is one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• The name Mohenjo-daro means "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi.
 
• The city was built around 2500 BCE and is known for its advanced urban planning and architecture.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**
 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, contemporaneous with the civilizations of ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.
 
• It flourished in the basins of the Indus River, which flows through present-day Pakistan and northwest India.
 
• The civilization is noted for its cities built of brick, roadside drainage systems, and multi-story houses.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Significance**
 
 
• The Great Bath is considered one of the earliest public water tanks in the ancient world.
 
• Its construction techniques, such as the use of bitumen for waterproofing, highlight the advanced engineering skills of the Indus Valley people.

questions.question: ‘Purusha Sukta’ is a hymn from which Veda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Rigveda.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Purusha Sukta’ is a hymn from Rigveda.**
 
• In the **10th Mandala** of the Rigveda, Purusha Sukta outlines the origin of the four varnas (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra) from different parts of Purusha’s body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Rig Veda**:

 
 
• Rig Veda was said to be composed between 1500-1200 B.C, also known as the first testament of mankind.
 
• It is a collection of 10,600 verses and 1,028 hymns.
 
• It consists of 10 books also known as mandalas, each Mandal consists of Suktas.
 
• It consists of various secrets about the origin of the universe, the origin of Lord Shiva, the origin of Lord Varuna, etc.

questions.question: The construction of the “Sanchi Stupa” was commissioned by which Mauryan Emperor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option **3**, i.e __**Ashoka**__.

__
 
• The Construction of the **"Sanchi Stupa"** was commissioned by **Ashoka.**
 
• It is situated at Sanchi Town in Raisen District of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is also a **UNESCO World heritage site.**
 
• Its **official name** is **Buddhist Monument at Sanchi.**
 
• Sanchi Stupa number 1 has a large number of Brahmi Inscription*.*
 
• **Bindusara** was the son of the dynasty's founder **Chandragupta**.
 
• **Kautilya** or Chanakya (c. 350 - 283 B.C.E.) was an adviser and a Prime Minister to the first Maurya Emperor Chandragupta.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

__
 
• With the help of Chanakya (Vishnugupta/ Kautilya), Chandragupta Maurya defeated Dhana Nanda (322 BCE) and founded the Mauryan Dynasty.
 
• Chanakya encouraged Chandragupta Maurya and his army to take over the throne of Magadha.
 
• His vast empire included Bihar, Bengal, Deccan (except modern Kerala, Tamilnadu, and parts of Northeast India), Eastern Afghanistan, Baluchistan, and the area west of the Indus river.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

bindusara

 
• Chandragupta was succeeded by his son Bindusara.
 
• Bindusara ruled for approximately 25-26 years and his succession was disputed which ultimately gave India a great king called Asoka.

Ashoka

 
• Asoka was the third and the greatest of the Mauryan rulers.
 
• Ashoka is referred to as Ashokavardhana.

Kunala

 
• Kunala was the son of Emperor Ashoka and Queen Padmavati and the presumptive heir to Ashoka.

questions.question: In 1336 A.D. who had established the Vijaynagar empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Vijayanagar Empire** was founded in 1336 A.D. by **Harihara I and Bukka Raya I,** collectively known as the Sangama brothers. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• They were originally commanders in the Kakatiya kingdom and later served the Delhi Sultanate, before declaring independence and establishing a sovereign Hindu kingdom in southern India.
 
• The empire was established on the banks of the Tungabhadra River in present-day Karnataka.
 
• The city of Vijayanagar (near modern-day Hampi) became a powerful and wealthy capital.

questions.question: Of the following, which one was written by Ziauddin Barani?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

__
 
• **Ziauddin Barani **was a 14th-century historian and political thinker during the Delhi Sultanate period.*** Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• **He is best known for two major works:**
 
 
• **Fatawa-i-Jahandari **– A political treatise discussing ideal governance, the role of the Sultan, and Muslim polity.
 
• **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi **– A historical chronicle of the Delhi Sultans, especially Ghiyasuddin Balban and Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Zain-ul-Akhbar** → Written by Abu Said Gardezi
 
• **Tarikh-i-Muhammadi **→ Written by Muhammad Bihamad Khani

questions.question: Shahjahan gave the title of 'Shah Iqbal' to which of his son ?
Who after conquering most part of northern India, took the title of "Shiladitya'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harsha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Harsha, also known as Harshavardhana, was a ruler of North India who reigned from **606 to 647 CE**.
 
• After ascending the throne of Thanesar, he consolidated his power and expanded his empire to include most parts of northern India.
 
• Harsha adopted the title "**Shiladitya**," which signifies a strong and virtuous ruler.
 
• He was known for his administrative capabilities and promotion of Buddhism and other religions during his reign.
 
• Harsha organized great assemblies at **Kannauj** and also patronized scholars like Banabhatta, the author of "Harshacharita."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harsha's Empire:**

 
 
• Harsha's empire extended from Punjab in the west to Bengal in the east and from the Himalayas in the north to the Narmada River in the south.
 
• Despite his vast empire, he was unable to conquer the Deccan region due to resistance from Pulakesin II of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Religion and Patronage:**
 
 
• Harsha was initially a follower of Hinduism but later embraced Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• He was a patron of scholars, monks, and institutions such as Nalanda University.
 
 
 
• **Banabhatta:**
 
 
• Banabhatta was Harsha’s court poet and wrote "Harshacharita," a biographical account of Harsha's reign.
 
• The text provides valuable insights into the political and social conditions of Harsha's era.
 
 
 
• **Chinese Pilgrim Xuanzang:**
 
 
• Xuanzang, a Chinese Buddhist monk, visited India during Harsha’s reign and documented his experiences in detail.
 
• His travelogue provides important historical accounts of Harsha's administration and the cultural landscape of India during that time.

questions.question: Albuquerque acquired Goa from __________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sultan of Bijapur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Afonso de Albuquerque**, the Portuguese viceroy, captured **Goa** from the **Sultan of Bijapur** in **1510**.
 
• The **Bijapur Sultanate** was one of the powerful kingdoms in the Deccan, and Goa was under its control before the Portuguese invasion.
 
• Albuquerque strategically chose Goa due to its **geographical location** and its importance as a **port city**.
 
• Goa became the **center of Portuguese India** and remained under their control for over 450 years.
 
• The Portuguese used Goa as a base to expand their influence in **India and Southeast Asia**.
 
• The capture of Goa marked the beginning of European colonial expansion in the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **British**__

 __
 
• The **British East India Company** established its control in India during the 17th and 18th centuries.
 
• The British were primarily focused on controlling trade routes and establishing ports like **Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras**.
 
• They did not have control over Goa, as it was under Portuguese rule until **1961**, when India annexed it.
 
 
 
• **Nawab of Hyderabad**__
 __
 
• The **Nizam of Hyderabad** ruled a significant part of southern India but never held Goa.
 
• Hyderabad was a princely state, and its territory was separate from the regions controlled by Portuguese or British India.
 
• The Nizam was known for his wealth and neutrality during the colonial era.
 
 
 
• **Krishnadevaraya**__
 
 
• **Krishnadevaraya** was a ruler of the **Vijayanagara Empire**, which was one of the most powerful empires in southern India during the early 16th century.
 
• Though his empire included a large part of southern India, Goa was not under his control during Albuquerque's invasion.
 
• Krishnadevaraya was known for his patronage of art, architecture, and literature, as well as his military conquests.
